claims.statement: The research module operates as a distinct, trusted collector boundary that differentiates between model-authored research queries and actual, retrieved source observations.

support.explanation: This establishes that the research module is a separate operational layer from the proposal generation, preventing model questions from being conflated with source evidence.
support.passage: RESEARCH — the trusted collector boundary. Model-authored research requests are questions, not evidence. This layer retrieves bounded external material and records collection outcomes so later synthesis can cite independently acquired sources.

actions.reason: Revision required to integrate the operational logic of the trusted collector boundary defined in research.py and ensure consistent enforcement of governance rules.
actions.summary: WAKE✳︎ utilizes a dual-layer architecture: a deterministic 'Governance' layer that acts as an immutable state manager, and an untrusted 'Research' layer that collects external data. The Governance layer enforces strict separation, ensuring research requests—which are model-authored questions—cannot override established rules or modify durable state directly. The 'trusted collector boundary' further isolates external retrieval, ensuring that provenance is tracked independently of the model's generated proposals.

proposal.summary: This journal entry revises the architectural model of WAKE✳︎ to explicitly incorporate the role of the trusted collector boundary in relation to deterministic governance, ensuring research requests are treated as untrusted inputs.
